subject: compound-interest
title: Money That Grows Money
summary: Compound interest: when your interest starts earning interest too.

cards.title: Money that grows on its own?
cards.text: Imagine putting $100 in a savings account and never adding another cent. Twenty-five years later, it could be almost $340. Where does the extra money come from?

cards.title: Interest is a thank-you
cards.text: When you keep money in a bank, the bank pays you a little extra for letting it use your money. That extra is called interest.
cards.example: If you have $100 and earn 5% interest in a year, you get $5. Now you have $105.

cards.title: Interest on interest
cards.text: In year two, you earn 5% on all $105, not just the first $100. That gives you $110.25. The extra 25 cents is interest earned on your interest. This is called compound interest.

cards.title: Small at first, big later
cards.text: Each year, the pile grows a little faster than the year before. After 10 years, $100 at 5% grows to more than $162. After 25 years, it is almost $340.
cards.example: The early years look slow. The later years are where it really takes off.

cards.title: Time is the secret ingredient
cards.text: The longer your money stays put, the more years it has to grow on itself. That is why starting early helps so much, even with small amounts.

cards.question: Besides money, what else gets bigger faster the longer you keep at it, like interest on interest?
nudges: Think about reading, practicing a sport, or making friends.
What happens if you stop and start over?

questions.q: You have $100 and earn 5% interest in one year. How much do you have?

options.why: That would be 50%. 5% of $100 is just $5.
That is only 5 cents. 5% of $100 is $5.

options.text: You earn interest on your interest, too.
options.why: Right. That is why it grows faster over time.

options.text: The bank takes money away each year.
options.why: With interest, the bank adds money to your account.

options.text: You get the same amount every single year.
options.why: That would be simple interest. Compound interest grows a bit more each year.

options.text: Your money has more years to grow on itself.
options.why: Yes. Time is the secret ingredient.
The rate is not about age. Time is what helps.
Starting early gives your money more time to grow.
